title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class mixed add/square rho on GT (v3)

claims.statement: For uniform z in GT and uniform nonidentity input (the challenge of rules.md), the algorithm in proof.md returns Q with e(P, Q) = z with probability at least 0.41 (model 0.410001), using at most 2^125.719085 target-group-operation equivalents (score 25143817/200000), including preprocessing (2^75.418470), the adder table, walk starts and restarts, cycle waste, distinguished-point storage, fingerprint verification, collision replay, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^73.166751 bytes. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Each walk step costs its group operations (one Fp12 multiplication charged 1, one cyclotomic squaring kappa = 0.4902) plus c2 = 0.1445 units of other work, measured by Callgrind on the organizer's blst build at the production square count. The bound rests on heuristics H1-H4 in proof.md. This is a classical generic attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the Frobenius-class mixed walk (cscore.gt) on toy order-ell subgroups of F_{q^12}^* with ell dividing q^4 - q^2 + 1, solve each instance end to end and verify g^y = z, and compare the success curve of tau = T^2 V / (2N) with 1 - exp(-tau), reporting cycle rates. Toy scale only: it tests H1 and the solver, not production cost.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters, the measured c2 and kappa, the measured cycle rate, and cscore.exact.
